newsitem.title: CANADA: CWB sold 250,000 T wheat to India for Feb - trade.
newsitem.headline: CWB sold 250,000 T wheat to India for Feb - trade.

text.p: The Canadian Wheat Board sold 250,000 tonnes of low-grade milling wheat to India for February arrival, grain trade sources said.

"They've done 250,000 tonnes for February. We believe they're working some additional but can't provide enough for the Indians. We have a price of US$152 to US$153 a tonne FOB Vancouver," one source said.
Australia sold 1.0 million tonnes of milling wheat to India last week.
Indian Food Minister Devendra Prasad Yadav said last Thursday India would import 2.0 million tonnes of wheat in fiscal 1996/97 (April/March) to augment domestic supplies and check rising prices.
The last time it imported that much wheat was in 1991/92.

"The tender was officially for arrival January 20th, which is impossible for the Board, it would mean December shipment. There's trade rumours of January and February shipment and it's probably low-grade milling wheat," another source said.
Asked about the industry talk of Monday's sale to India, CWB spokeswoman Tracey Thompson said, "We neither confirm nor deny any sale."
